notes.summary: Probability measures how likely an event is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). JSO questions use classical probability (coins, dice, cards), addition and multiplication theorems, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem.

concepts.title: Basic ideas
concepts.body:
• Classical: P(A) = favourable outcomes / total equally likely outcomes.
  • 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1; P(A') = 1 − P(A).
  • Two coins: 4 outcomes; two dice: 36 outcomes; a deck: 52 cards (4 suits × 13; 4 aces, 12 face cards).
  • Mutually exclusive: cannot happen together, P(A∩B) = 0. Independent: P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B).

concepts.title: Theorems
concepts.body:
• Addition: P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A∩B).
  • Multiplication: P(A∩B) = P(A) × P(B|A).
  • Conditional: P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B).
  • At least one of independent events = 1 − P(none happens).
  • Bayes': P(Ei|A) = P(Ei)P(A|Ei) / Σ P(Ej)P(A|Ej).

varieties.name: Coins, dice and cards
varieties.how: Count the sample space and the favourable cases; use the complement for "at least one".

example.q: Two dice are thrown. Find P(sum = 7).

varieties.name: Addition and multiplication theorems
varieties.how: OR → add and subtract the overlap; AND → multiply (use conditional probability when drawing without replacement).

example.q: P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5, A and B independent. Find P(A∪B).

varieties.name: Conditional probability and Bayes'
varieties.how: Make a table of P(source) × P(event | source); the answer is one row divided by the total.

example.q: Bag I: 3 red, 2 black. Bag II: 2 red, 3 black. A bag is chosen at random and a red ball is drawn. Find P(Bag I | red).

tips: "At least one" problems are fastest with 1 − P(none).
Without replacement, the second draw's denominator falls by one.
In Bayes' questions, write the prior × likelihood products first; the denominator is their sum.
traps: Mutually exclusive events (with non-zero probabilities) are NOT independent.
Do not forget to subtract P(A∩B) in the addition theorem.
P(A|B) is not the same as P(B|A).

questions.q: Two fair coins are tossed. The probability of getting at least one head is:
questions.solution:
Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT. Only TT has no head.
P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.

questions.q: A fair die is thrown. The probability of getting a number greater than 4 is:
questions.solution:
Numbers greater than 4: 5 and 6, i.e. 2 out of 6.
P = 2/6 = 1/3.
